_note: What an answer from the stand MEANS (RH1-7, AR-1: closed variety is a data row). Read by env_probe.stand_answers() - the one reader; stand_health reads it through env_probe. `codes`: first match wins; a row matches by `codes` (a list) or `from`..`to` (inclusive) or `any`, and by `kinds` (the answer's http_client kind must be one of them) / `not_kinds` (must not be one; a bare status with no kind is in no `kinds` list and in every `not_kinds` complement). `verdict` is the word env_probe.liveness has always used (alive | wants_login | dead); `means` is what the answer is; `note` is the suffix of the liveness note ({said}, {described} are filled from the classified body); `direct` = words when the API's own address answered this way; `through_frontend` = `class` (api = the API itself wrote it | unknown | config | upstream | api_error) and words when the frontend's API path answered this way. `no_answer`: class NAMES of the exception (one unwrap of URLError.reason first), matched through the class hierarchy - the most specific listed ancestor wins - then the row with `fallback: OSError` for any other OSError, then the row with `fallback: other`. `run_evidence: true` (RH2-9, read by s5_precheck.check_env_evidence through env_probe.stand_answers): the row's `names` are exception names whose appearance in a failed run's own error line is evidence of the stand (a refused or dropped connection, a name that does not resolve, a refused handshake); a row without it is not (`timeout`: a test's own wait expiring is not the stand). `order`: the dependency order walked by ONE loop in stand_health._diagnose; each check goes to the first row (by `order`) that takes its role and tag; `needs: api` = the row says `unknown` when no API address is probed; `chain: false` = a part outside the stand's chain (the sentence keeps its older wording). `login_remedies`: the remedy by the recorded login code; `login_recheck`: the one command that re-checks the login. Words use {url} {host} {code} {path} {name} {note}. A missing or unreadable file never makes a stand alive: liveness then says `dead` (table_unreadable).

login_remedies.remedy: Check the body field names environment.access.user_field / secret_field (the endpoint may want other fields), or the account in {user_key}.
Check the account or its secret: the values of {user_key} and of the secret key in the env file (their values are never shown).
Look at the stand, not the login: python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/stand_health.py" --probe.

login_recheck: python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/env_probe.py" --project-root . --json and record its login.record as environment.access.login_probe

remedy.with_recipe: Restarting is the conductor's move when it is authorized; the recorded recipe (environments[{name}].bring_up): {recipe}
remedy.no_recipe: No restart recipe is recorded for this stand (environments[].bring_up).

texts.frontend_not_cause: The frontend is not the cause: its route to the API fails because the API itself does not answer.
texts.contradiction: The frontend reaches an API at its own upstream that the configured API address does not: the two addresses may name different backends.
texts.api_not_configured: The API's own address is not configured: whether the API or the frontend's route is dead cannot be told.
texts.table_unreadable: The answer table could not be read (references/stand-answers.json), so the answers of the stand cannot be told apart.
texts.frontend_unset: frontend configured but {key} is not set
texts.frontend_not_http: frontend configured but {key} is not an http address
texts.api_path_bad: frontend.api_path is not a path starting with one / - it is not probed

login_not_tried.not_recorded: the access scheme is not recorded
